title: US Dollar Shortage and the Cross-Currency Basis

maps.tested: Rated Very Important and reported as an explicit theory question.
maps.specifics: Reported verbatim: 'why non-US banks faced dollar shortage during GFC.' The mechanism, dollar-denominated assets funded by short-term wholesale dollar liabilities without a dollar deposit base or Fed access, is the answer. Covered interest parity and the cross-currency basis (Reading 82) is the adjacent reading.

vardeezReading: LTR-15: Very Important; "Short Reading and anything can be tested here - so know it well". LTR-16: Important; the same note, "Short Reading and anything can be tested here - so know it well".

selectors.name: Why non-US banks faced a dollar shortage
selectors.what: Why non-US (chiefly European) banks faced a US dollar shortage in the GFC: long dollar assets funded by short-term wholesale dollar liabilities and FX swaps, with no dollar deposit base and no Fed access, so that the maturity mismatch widened as interbank, swap and money market fund funding dried up while assets could not be shed. It was not a domestic bank run, and foreign currency is special because home central banks cannot create dollars.

selectors.name: CIP violations and the cross-currency basis
selectors.what: Covered interest parity F/S = (1 + r)/(1 + r*) (S and F in USD per unit of foreign currency) and its violation, the cross-currency basis b = (F - S)/S - (r - r*): its sign (a negative EUR or JPY basis means swapped dollars cost more than cash dollars), the factors that move it (illiquidity, credit risk, risk premium, FX hedging demand) and why it persisted after 2014 (hedging demand meeting balance sheet costs and limits to arbitrage).
selectors.theory: What the basis measures as a CIP deviation, which hedgers (banks, institutional investors, non-financial issuers) keep it negative or positive, and why arbitrage does not close it: balance sheet space is rented, not free.

notSelected: LTR-15 b (assessing maturity and currency mismatches on the consolidated rather than residency balance sheet), LTR-15 c (the Fed swap lines and their effectiveness) and LTR-16 a (FX swap versus cross-currency swap mechanics) carry a bare Vardeez focus flag only and no shape, Map point or Vardeez pointer of their own.
